grand_strategy.reading: Male buys time with money, not force. The India Out campaign of 2023-24 ended in a debt-driven repair with New Delhi, which now lends the currency reserves and the credit lines, while China stays the largest bilateral creditor and the source of defence assistance and a trade deal in force since 2025. Tourism is the economy that pays for both, which makes the state hostage to the arrivals it must keep open, and the sea that threatens it is the argument for every climate loan it asks for. Its line is to be useful to every big lender at once; its paradox is that the campaign against Indian presence brought India's money back in.

stances.note: Mirror of India's own card (IND to MDV). After India Out (2023-24) the Maldives repaired ties for money: the USD 400m and INR 30bn swaps of October 2024, a INR 4,850 crore credit line (about USD 565m) announced in Malé on 25-26 July 2025 during Modi's visit, and the INR 30bn drawdown of April 2026. Warming because India is the lender of last resort; China is the competing pull. Bond none: pure interest. Sources: the Wire (2024-10), Atoll Times (2026-04), Al Jazeera (2025-07-25).

The China-Maldives FTA entered into force on 1 January 2025; China's bilateral debt-relief arrangement was finalised in October 2025, terms unpublished. Partner, not ally: the defence assistance is reported through secondary sources and the text of the defence agreement was not seen (confidence B on the rest). Bond none: the link is debt, trade and assistance, not kinship or affinity. Trend warming on the Maldivian side; India remains the lender of last resort.

stances.note: Former protecting power, now a Commonwealth partner. The UK opened a call for input on a goods-only free trade agreement in June 2023 and the Maldives asked for an agreement to cut fish tariffs. The FTA has not been concluded; the second strategic dialogue (May 2025) drew opposition complaints that it was missing. Partner, not reluctant: no visible friction. Confidence C: the only source is a tier-3 report of the talks launch; no source reads the relationship as partnership in those words. Bond none. The Chagos maritime boundary with the British Indian Ocean Territory is undemarcated (Wikipedia index, not checked).

stances.note: Recognises the State of Palestine since 1988 (dataset row). The Gaza war made Palestine the public axis of Male's foreign policy: the June 2024 announcement of an entry ban on Israeli passport holders was framed by the government as a response to Israel's conduct against Palestinians, and enacted in 2025 in conditional form. Partner (cooperation without alignment), not ally: there is no treaty and no reported military or financial tie. Bond kin: a shared Sunni Muslim identity, the Maldives being an Islamic republic in the OIC. Confidence C: solidarity is government framing; the grade is our reading of the structure.
